text: You hit 'update' for a small bug fix. Your device downloads a massive file, gigabytes for a tiny tweak. You just want that specific change, not the whole application.
It feels like developers send everything. You wonder why they can't just send the changed parts. Surely, there's a smarter way to deliver small updates, right?
Your initial thought: send only 'diffs' – just byte-level differences. But even this perfect calculation has hidden complexities for distribution and installation.
The real system tracks every file change. For updates, they often send entire modified files or even bundles. This ensures integrity and faster installation.
This means larger downloads and more bandwidth. The cost is a bigger burden on your internet and storage. Your illusion of 'small parts' is broken by practical needs.
Next time you see a huge update, you’ll understand the trade-off. It's a system designed for reliability and speed, even if it means bigger files.
